h1: China visa-free 2027: will UK travellers still need a visa?
intro: Latest update, 25 November 2026: China still hasn’t said whether visa-free entry for British passport holders will continue after 31 December 2026. On 17 November, its Foreign Ministry said only that it is studying the policy. We check official announcements every day and will update this page the same day a decision is made. Here’s where China visa-free 2027 travel stands, who still needs a visa, and how to plan a January trip so you’re not caught out.

sections.heading: The current visa-free rules
sections.text:
Since 17 February 2026, holders of ordinary British passports can enter mainland China without a visa for up to 30 days for:
- tourism
- business
- visiting family and friends
- transit

The scheme runs until 31 December 2026. It doesn’t cover work, study or journalism, which still need the right visa.

sections.heading: Who still needs a China visa, whatever happens
sections.text:
Even if the scheme is extended, you’ll still need a visa if you’re:
- staying in China for more than 30 days
- going to work, study or report as a journalist (Z, X or J visa)
- joining family for a longer stay (Q or S visa)
- living in the UK on a non-British passport
- travelling on a Home Office travel document (for example a refugee travel document), which isn’t an ordinary British passport

Visa-free entry depends on the passport you hold, not where you live. For example, UK residents with Indian, Pakistani, Nigerian or Bangladeshi passports usually still need a visa. We prepare these applications every week from our Manchester office. See our [China visa service](/china-visa-application/).

sections.heading: China visa-free 2027: has it been extended?
sections.text:
Not yet. As of 25 November 2026, China hasn’t announced an extension for British citizens, or for any of the other 47 countries in the same scheme, including France, Germany, Spain, Italy, Australia and Japan. All of them are due to lose visa-free entry at midnight Beijing time on 31 December 2026.

At its regular press briefing on 17 November, China’s Foreign Ministry was asked directly whether the scheme would be extended. Spokesperson Guo Jiakun said China values making travel easier and is “seriously studying the relevant policy”, but gave no decision and no date.

For comparison, last year’s extension was announced on 3 November 2025, so this year’s decision is already later than last time. An extension is still possible, and China has a track record of renewing the scheme. But nothing is confirmed, and you shouldn’t book a January trip on the assumption that it will happen.

We’re watching official announcements and will update this page and our [visa news](/news/) page as soon as anything changes.

sections.heading: No China visa-free 2027 decision yet: if you’re travelling in January
sections.text:
If no extension is announced, you’ll need a Chinese visa for trips starting on or after 1 January 2027. For most holidays and family visits, that’s an L (tourist) visa. For business trips, it’s an M visa. Visas are applied for online and then at a Chinese Visa Application Service Centre, where you give fingerprints and hand in your passport.

If you’re travelling in the first half of January, don’t wait for the announcement. The visa centre advises submitting your online application at least 30 days before you travel, and it closes for public holidays over Christmas and New Year. In practice that means:
- travelling 1 to 10 January: start your application now, and aim to submit by early December
- travelling later in January: start by mid-December
- travelling in February or later: you can wait a little longer for China’s decision, but don’t leave it until the last minute, as Chinese New Year is busy

If China does extend visa-free entry after you’ve applied, a visa is still useful: it can be valid for longer than 30 days, and some visas allow several trips.

sections.heading: Another option: 240-hour visa-free transit
sections.text: British citizens can also use China’s 240-hour visa-free transit. It lets you stay up to 10 days if you’re travelling on to a third country, for example London to Shanghai to Tokyo. You need a confirmed onward ticket, must enter and leave through one of 65 designated ports, and stay within the permitted provinces. It isn’t available for a return trip straight back to the UK.

sections.heading: Travelling over new year
sections.text: If you enter China visa-free before 31 December 2026 and plan to stay into January, check your plans carefully before you travel, as China visa-free 2027 rules haven’t been confirmed. Make sure you’ll leave within 30 days of entering, and check the latest guidance, as the rules for stays that cross the end date haven’t been spelled out in detail.

sections.heading: How we can help
sections.text: We’ve been processing Chinese visas from our Manchester office since 2007. If you need a visa because there’s no China visa-free 2027 extension in time for your trip, we can complete your online form, check your documents and get your application ready for the visa centre. See our [China visa service](/china-visa-application/), or read our guide to [China visa-free travel for British citizens](/blog/china-visa-free-british-citizens-2026/).

faqs.q: Is China visa-free for UK citizens in 2027?
faqs.a: Not unless China extends the scheme. It’s currently due to end on 31 December 2026, and no extension has been announced.

faqs.q: Has China said whether it will extend visa-free entry?
faqs.a: Not yet. On 17 November 2026, China’s Foreign Ministry said it is studying the policy, but gave no decision or date. We’ll update this page as soon as an announcement is made.

faqs.q: I live in the UK but don’t have a British passport. Can I go to China visa-free?
faqs.a: Only if your own passport is on China’s visa-free list. Many UK residents aren’t covered and need a visa. Tell us your nationality and we’ll confirm.

faqs.q: When should I apply for a China visa for January 2027?
faqs.a: Now, if you travel in early January. The visa centre advises applying at least 30 days before travel and closes over Christmas and New Year, so don’t wait for China’s decision.

faqs.q: Can I use 240-hour transit instead of a visa?
faqs.a: Only if you’re travelling on to a third country with a confirmed onward ticket. It doesn’t work for a return trip to the UK.

faqs.q: Does visa-free entry cover business trips?
faqs.a: Yes, business meetings and similar activities are covered for up to 30 days until 31 December 2026. Paid work isn’t.

faqs.q: How long does a China visa take from the UK?
faqs.a: Usually about four working days after your appointment at the visa centre, with faster express options available for an extra fee. Allow extra time around the new year and Chinese New Year.

faqs.q: Do I need a visa if I only change planes in China?
faqs.a: Usually not, if you stay airside and have a confirmed onward ticket. Check with your airline before you fly.
